articles.title: ‘Charming and disarming’ … how Meta’s technology-packed Muse harnesses the power of cuteness
articles.summary: The tech giant has launched a cute ‘little guy’ that can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop. After the recent backlash against Meta’s so-called “pervert” smart glasses, this week Mark Zuckerberg launched a much cuter alternative: the Muse “charm” device.
body: With a screen that shows a cutesy little avatar, it has drawn comparisons with Tamagotchis. “We’ve packed a lot of technology into this little guy,” the Meta founder told the San Francisco audience.

The “little guy” could fit, like a Labubu, on to a keychain or bag. But unlike a Labubu, the interactive AI assistant will have significant capabilities, including the ability to have live conversations. It can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop.

According to Katie Seaborn, a Cambridge associate professor who has been researching cuteness – creating the science of cute voices within the context of computing – it’s cute because it “basically looks like a baby”.

For Joshua Paul Dale, professor at Chuo University in Tokyo and author of Irresistible: How Cuteness Wired our Brains and Conquered the World: “It’s really significant that along with the wearable charm, Meta also introduced a new pair of smart glasses with no camera. Everyone hates cameras in smart glasses. But if the camera is contained in a charm you wear around your neck, it shifts the agency. Suddenly, you’re not recording people. It’s just a cute little animated avatar looking out on the world.”
points: The tech giant has launched a cute ‘little guy’ that can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop.

articles.title: Dolce & Gabbana mixes it up as pressure mounts for turnaround
articles.summary: With Jennifer Lopez providing some star power, the Italian house’s Milan show came at a crucial time for the brand. Earlier this week Jennifer Lopez walked down the Vogue World catwalk in Milan wearing a black beaded A-line bustier dress from Dolce & Gabbana.
body: The reminder of Dolce & Gabbana ’s inimitable celebrity connection is no coincidence. In a turbulent luxury market, the brand has found itself trying to navigate a nearly £400m debt pile.
In August, the company, embroiled in controversy over the years, reached an agreement with its banks that gave it until March 2028 to settle its debt.
In exchange for the waiver, the brand must carry out a series of “extraordinary corporate transactions”, which reportedly include the sale of some of its properties.
It is one of the few fashion houses that remains independent. Gucci and Bottega Veneta are owned by the French conglomerate Kering while Fendi has been absorbed by LVMH.

articles.title: ‘I was mesmerised by how the fog turned the tower into a monolith’: Derek Zhao’s best phone picture
articles.summary: Zhao was out jogging around Treasure Island, near San Francisco, when he spotted a lonely tower stabbing through the clouds. Every morning, Derek Zhao jogs the perimeter of Treasure Island, his home, situated an eight-minute ferry ride from San Francisco.
body: Zhao works as a machine-learning engineer at Disney California. He relocated from Texas last year to take up the role, finding the 400-acre human-made island to be the perfect location, “close enough to the office and all the culture the city has to offer, but far enough that I’m waking up to the sound of seagulls instead of car horns”.

He took this image earlier this year, stopping mid-jog to capture the top of San Francisco’s Salesforce Tower. “I was mesmerised by how the fog, caused by what’s known as a marine layer, completely covered the rest of the skyline, leaving only the tower looking like a monolith,” he says. “It’s ironic that something that obscures, like fog, can make a scene more clear.”

It’s only recently that Zhao has come to realise that his favourite photos don’t come from travels with his professional cameras, but “improbable scenes near home that somehow only reveal themselves when I’m not expecting them. It brings me considerable peace that despite living in such close proximity to the centre of things I feel ambivalent about – tech, AI, urban density, hustle culture – the universe can still grant such awe-inspiring moments of quiet.

articles.title: Inside Dove Cameron’s Final Fitting for Her “Celestial” Valentino Wedding Dress in Rome
articles.summary: See a first look at Dove Cameron’s custom Valentino wedding dress here, shared exclusively with Vogue. The musician and actor tied the knot with former Måneskin frontman Damiano David in a ceremony in Tuscany this weekend.
body: Dove Cameron and Damiano David are officially married! As shared exclusively with Vogue, the couple tied the knot this weekend at a private ceremony in Tuscany—and just four days before the wedding weekend celebrations, we joined Dove in Rome to pay a visit to the Valentino ateliers in Rome and try on her wedding dress for the very last time.

“Ciao, Vogue!” the musician and actor says before the final fitting, sitting at an outdoor café and reflecting on the experience of planning the wedding. “I never really dreamed about what my wedding would look like when I was a little girl—I think I wanted to rent out Carnegie Hall and enter in a big, black dress made out of feathers and have a 32-piece orchestra playing,” she says. And while she jokingly describes herself as “wildly unprepared” for the wedding ahead, she also notes: “It feels right. It feels natural. It feels easy. It feels like a natural, beautiful next step. I don't know how else to describe it. I'm in love, [and] we're throwing a big party.”

articles.title: Apple Slab Pie
articles.summary: There’s almost nothing that signals fall to me like the smell of an apple pie baking in my kitchen. And when that’s happening there’s a high likelihood I’ll be gathering with friends and family in the near future because, well, pies are meant to be shared!While I love a traditional lattice-topped…
body: I’ve spent more than a decade developing and styling recipes for all things sweet, starting in the Martha Stewart Living test kitchen, where meticulously perfected pies were in constant rotation no matter the time of year. I’m a big believer in approachable desserts that deliver maximum impact with minimal fuss, and this sizable pie checks all the right boxes. It feels special enough for a holiday, but still simple enough for a casual gathering.
Dice 4 1/2 sticks cold unsalted butter. Divide into 4 portions (4 1/2 ounces each), and refrigerate until ready to use.
Pulse 2 3/4 cups of the all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 teaspoons of the granulated sugar, and 1 teaspoon kosher salt together in a food processor a few times to combine.
Scatter 1 portion of the butter cubes over the flour. Pulse until the butter is cut into pieces no larger than a pea, about 10 (1-second) pulses.

articles.title: The Most Delicious Beef Stew of All Time
articles.summary: Editor’s Note: If you’ve cooked this beloved recipe before, it might look a little different these days! We recently improved it to make it even easier to follow and more delicious.There are few meals more comforting than a big pot of something slowly simmering away on the stove — especially when…
body: A rich, comforting beef stew with tender chunks of beef, hearty vegetables, fresh herbs, and a deeply savory, flavorful gravy.

The potatoes and carrots go in toward the end so they become perfectly tender without turning mushy, and a handful of peas adds a pop of sweetness and color. Best of all, once everything is simmering, the heat does most of the work for you. Serve this stew straight from the pot with plenty of crusty bread or on a bed of mashed potatoes with a sprinkling of fresh chopped parsley. It is the coziest, most satisfying dinner that makes the long simmer completely worth the wait.

After attending two culinary schools, I’ve spent more than a decade working behind the scenes in test kitchens and on some of America’s favorite cooking shows. I love developing approachable recipes that are easy enough for a weeknight but still feel special and deliver big flavor without making cooking feel like rocket science.
This beef stew can be made up to 1 day in advance. Let cool, then cover and refrigerate. Reheat over medium heat, stirring occasionally until warmed through.

articles.title: Comedian Edy Modica Is Just Like You (But Funnier)
articles.summary: It’s been a busy few years for Modica, who just released her first stand-up special, “I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks).”
body: When comedian Edy Modica arrives at the Condé Nast offices in downtown Manhattan, she looks as if she’s just wrapped filming on a Bravo show—her hoop earrings are sparkly and huge, her heeled denim boots coordinate perfectly with her long denim shorts, and a nameplate necklace spells out EDY. As I soon learn, that is, in fact, exactly the case; Modica is coming straight from guest-bartending on an episode of Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen.

Modica is promoting I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks), her chatty, confrontational, and sometimes crude debut special. (One of its best parts revolves around a young Modica browsing sites with names like “boobs.com” and “sex.com.”) But her strong and singular comedic voice has remained largely unchanged since I saw her perform a fully nude show at Williamsburg’s now-shuttered Annoyance Theatre a decade ago. I struggle with how to bring it up without sounding like a pervert, but Modica excitedly tells me that she remembers the set well; in fact, both of her parents were in attendance.
points: It’s been a busy few years for Modica, who just released her first stand-up special, “I’m Just Like You (And It Sucks).”

articles.title: A Professional Chef Swears By This 2-Step Method for the Crispiest Chicken Wings
articles.summary: Esther Choi has her hand in many pots. She’s an award-winning chef, restaurant owner, cookbook author, Food Network host, and now creator of Sessy, her own brand of condiments. And her Korean roots have had a huge influence on all of it.
body: Her pantry is always stocked with rice, gochujang, and soy sauce — the latter two from her own range. “Growing up in my halmoni’s (Korean for grandmother’s) kitchen and running NYC restaurants taught me that Korean cooking starts with the foundations. So I created Sessy, launching with gochujang, sesame oil, and soy sauce, the building blocks of Korean cuisine,” Choi says. The inspiration behind the name? “Sessy is sexy and sassy, just like my energy in the kitchen.”

Korean cuisine features an array of flavors, textures, and techniques. Choi enjoys cooking for family and friends, and their favorite dish is hands-down her kimchi jjigae. You can find the Korean dishes she grew up making with her grandmother and more in her upcoming cookbook, Hand Taste, launching on October 27.

articles.title: From Gucci to Gelato—How Shawn Mendes Does Milan Fashion Week
articles.summary: “I loved the big puffy jackets,” says the singer of the new Gucci show he attended.
body: Since wrapping his On The Road Again tour last year, the Canadian singer has since been enjoying some well-deserved R&R off the stage—quietly building a life with new girlfriend Bruna Marquezine, of course. “I’ve been really great,” Mendes tells Vogue of how he spent his summer. “I’ve been spending my time doing something I never really have before—building a life, community, and home outside of my career.”

This week, however, Mendes was ready for a little fashion fun again: He and Marquezine attended the Gucci spring 2027 show during Milan Fashion Week. A fitting move, given that Mendes stars in the Italian label’s new Primavera campaign. (Admit it, you’ve seen the photos of Mendes wearing a skin-tight shirt.) It may not have been Mendes’s first time in Milan this week, but he says this trip had a whole different energy to it. “Honestly, this time it felt completely different,” says Mendes. “I felt like it was the first time I was really able to see how absolutely beautiful and thoughtful of a city Milan is.”

articles.title: Poet Doireann Ní Ghríofa on Her Searching New Book, ‘Said the Dead’
articles.summary: In “Said the Dead,” we meet and follow extraordinary women with extraordinary lives, in a time when Europe and Ireland are in the midst of World War I. As infectious disease outbreaks tear through a women’s asylum in Cork City, Lucia Strangman, one of Europe’s first female doctors, rises to these…
body: Said the Dead, Ní Ghríofa’s new book, starts with a small confusion in her public library’s archives—a book slip is sent to an old address. A realtor phones to complain, a call that eventually brings Ní Ghríofa, “on a whim,” to wander Cork Mental Hospital, what was, on opening in the 1850s, one of the largest asylums in Europe. By 2020, however, it had been reduced to a century-and-a-half-old ruin running a mile along the River Lee and in the midst of condo conversion.

If it all sounds harrowing, that’s because it is, but the poetry of the book leads us forward in ways that remind us how grief is not so much something that individuals or even cities resolve, but that we carry forward, allowing us to feel life more deeply. In that spirit, the myriad voices the reader encounters aren’t so much confused at the close of Said the Dead as overlapping, like waves in the sea, and we maybe feel the urge to write ourselves a better life, and in so doing, direct others. “If you take the next step,” one voice says, “you leave here and make a path so others can come—others who need help—but they will only find me if you write them a map.”

articles.title: These Easy French Toast Sticks Are Better Than the Frozen Ones I Grew Up On
articles.summary: Breakfast when I was a kid had so much whimsy and excitement to it. I often found myself eager in anticipation of what we were having. Are those cinnamon rolls I smell in the oven? Are we making pancakes this weekend? Nowadays, breakfast doesn’t have the same ring to it.
body: I just made our French toast sticks recipe and was taken back to those days of fun, sweet breakfasts. I don’t know why I don’t fill my mornings with maple syrup and powdered sugar more often! Here’s how you can turn the traditional French toast breakfast into an easy grab-and-go option.

Anyone can whip up French toast, but serving French toast sticks is even more fun. The bite-size version of the breakfast classic is convenient to eat on the go, or serve as a side at a potluck brunch. Personally, I never really finish a whole slice of French toast, so grabbing just a stick or two is the perfect amount on my plate.

Plus, French toast sticks cover more surface area in sweet, egg-battered, fried goodness. My chief complaint about traditional French toast is that it can get soggy, but these sticks stay crispy. The short soak time in the egg mixture helps, and so does frying each side of the stick. You’ll also want to start with dry bread or toast your bread.

articles.title: She Shared Her Mom’s Best Room-Freshening Trick, and Now I’m Copying Her
articles.summary: It seems that the older I get, the more I dislike air fresheners. It’s nothing personal — it’s just that the vast majority of them are too strong, too artificial, and tend to leave me with a headache.But of course, I want the spaces I’m in to smell nice and eliminate odors, and I think I’ve just…
body: In a video by Wyoming-based content creator Caroline Goguen, she explains that one of the best hacks her mom ever taught her was to “put little bars of soap in sachet bags, stick them in your drawers, hang them in your closet, tuck them next to sweaters.” She adds that it “makes your clothes smell so fresh all the time.”
Plus, the dainty white oval in its sheer, pearly drawstring bag just looks nice. And if that’s not your aesthetic, bar soap comes in so many colors, shapes, and scents — so you’ve got options.

Not only is this a great way to keep your clothes smelling fresh, but its also a great way to keep any area of your home odor-free. Goguen and her mom aren’t the only ones to use this hack, either. Back in 2011, a writer for the blog Lifehacker explained that when he was 12 years old, he acquired a scented bar of soap and forgot about it in his bedroom. Within days, he noticed his room “started to smell really good,” and months later he realized it was the soap’s doing.
points: It seems that the older I get, the more I dislike air fresheners.
